bug_semantics: Renovate's npm manager generateLockFile() builds lockfile-update commands as single shell strings. User-influenced packageName values (and workspace directory names) are concatenated into `npm install ...` without quoting. util/exec spawn() forces shell:true, so shell metacharacters in packageName execute as commands on the Renovate host. Attackers with repository write access can set a malicious packageName (PoC: renovate.json5 packageRules.overridePackageName = "; kill 1; echo ") and trigger lockfile updates. First-party GHSA-fr4j-65pv-gjjj and CVE-2026-76230 both name this packageName injection; affected >=35.63.0 <40.33.0; patched in 40.33.0 by shlex quote() around workspace and packageKey tokens.
flaw_origin: The npm workspaces feature (PR #21274) first constructed per-workspace `npm install --workspace=${workspace} ${specs}` commands with unsanitized interpolation. Member 45881c2dd90702a9d0986a90f84931b6825c8dd5 introduced the unquoted --workspace= sink but still interpolated depName@version (the pre-existing root lockfile-update pattern). The CVE-named mechanism — appending packageName rather than depName into those shell strings — was first written in member 342a5069804f19d0af439f22855e9ee05cf7e223, which changed both workspace and root updateCmd maps from `update.depName@update.newVersion` to `update.packageName@update.newVersion`. Later members of the same PR wrapped that into generatePackageKey()/managerData.packageKey. GitHub squash-merged the PR as 012c0ac2fe32832e60a62bde405c0a241efd314c (35.63.0~2). overridePackageName (a70a6a376d31148e80be5a5c885ac33ff5ddb30c, 38.120.0) later made the PoC trivial but did not create the sink.
